pillar_reactions.evidence: She had pre-sold herself on the mechanism before the pillar was delivered — 'I really am intrigued by the idea of the kettlebells, because they are such full-body workouts' and 'I really like the idea that you guys combine flexibility with strength training.' After the rep delivered the pillar she answered 'Yes, yeah. Absolutely.' and tied it back to her own hip and glute stiffness.

The rep framed it as light tweaks on an already-good diet plus an intermittent-fasting protocol. She agreed without questions — 'Yeah, sounds good' — and had already volunteered that she responds well to fasted training: 'I tend to respond very well to exercising in a fasted state.'

Immediate agreement on delivery ('Okay, sounds good') and she engaged specifically with form review — 'Especially on the form part, because I did play around with him a little bit, but I didn't feel really confident that I was doing it correctly.' But she returned to it after the price as an open question: 'is it going to be enough interaction to make me accountable?', explicitly measuring it against the automated app that 'just sent you like a ping' and never responded.

anchors.raw: the little link that I got initially, it said it was like $119 a month or something.
anchors.note: The undercutting anchor is Primal Instinct's own low-tier product, delivered to her by the setter before the closing call. She converted it to a direct comparison against $6,000 in the same breath as computing '$1,000 a month'. Self-inflicted anchoring: the setter's link set a $119/mo expectation roughly fifty times below the offer, and the closer had to spend time dismantling his own company's cheaper product.

anchors.raw: I think it was around $3,000 or something like that. It was quite a bit to me, and then I didn't have any benefit whatsoever.
anchors.note: A prior online fitness app at roughly $3,000 that delivered nothing. This is a negative reference price rather than a competitive one: it establishes both that she can find $3,000 for a fitness product and that spending at that level has already failed her once. It is the single largest drag on the close — she returned to it three separate times and it was still unresolved at the end.

anchors.raw: when I was doing weight training, was only doing it twice a week with a personal trainer and for 30 minutes, twice a week... I was in the best shape of my life.
anchors.note: An established habit of paying for one-to-one coaching, with a good outcome attached. She also used him as the quality benchmark — 'He had a lot of women clients. He was very good at scaling stuff down' — so he supports the price of coaching in principle while raising the bar the remote coach has to clear.

unmet_demand.want: A coach with demonstrable experience programming for older, postmenopausal women — she raised female physiology explicitly: 'We are very different physiologically. We don't respond to things the same way that men do.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep conceded the shortfall directly: 'Trevor's experience with women is indeed a little bit less than with men... overall, like 95% of the people that he works with are men.' He substituted injury-rehab experience for female-specific experience, which does not answer the question she asked.

unmet_demand.want: Marketing and social proof that speaks to women — 'all of the ads and everything are very male-centric.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No female case study, testimonial or programming example was offered at any point, and the rep did not dispute the characterisation.

unmet_demand.want: A written statement of deliverables before committing — 'do you have a written plan of, okay, if you do this, this is what you get?'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme evidently does deliver these components; there is simply no document. The rep agreed to assemble a list on the spot ('I can send you the list of everything that we, well, would actually then do'), which means it did not exist as a standing asset.

unmet_demand.want: Confidence that the programme can be scaled for a 62-year-old restarting after ankle reconstruction — 'You can't start out like, you know, a 20-something.'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme almost certainly does scale — the rep cited a client who just had knee surgery and one about to have surgery — but the only evidence offered was the rep's own assertion, and he acknowledged as much: 'it comes down to if you believe my words.'
